parent.behavior_scope: accepted one local spare, explicit 10-minute REMOVE and 20-minute REPLACE, and inherited direct item repair

source.source_boundary: The traditional Item FRT supplies the complete System FRT for one installed LRU. A system SURP demand consumes a local spare; the removed LRU reaches ItemRepair at the end of REMOVE, then a repaired item serves future demands or returns to local stock.

delta.mechanism: Increase paired system and item OPHOURS FRT from 300000 to 450000 per million to elicit a second local LRU demand after the first removed item has completed its inherited one-hour direct repair and restocked.

predeclared_native_acceptance: The frozen seed/configuration must produce at least two observed installed-LRU failures and two system replacement demands; exact stochastic times are read from native events.

The first removed item must complete local ItemRepair and return to stock before the second demand. The second demand must issue that same repaired item identity, with stock on-hand conservation and no backorder at the two issue times.

For every observed failure, trace mission impact, demand and issued spare identity, explicit REMOVE then REPLACE, system recovery, removed-item direct repair and restock. Do not silently ignore an additional failure.

Import/export must preserve all 20 row-containing source tables, including three all-null placeholders; conversion errors must be zero, four native CLI steps must succeed and 72 half-hour system/stock result intervals must reconcile with raw events.

Compare against accepted E01 one-demand control, identifying added fault, repair, mission and stock effects. Use session-0 SSH under the host-wide native queue, preserve GUI PID 13340, seal raw hashes and obtain independent read-only replay.
limits: This is one local repair and reissue loop with sufficient time before the second demand; no shortage, late repair/backorder, remote transport, reorder, resource contention or PM behavior is accepted.
The 450000 FRT is a failure-rate input, not a prescribed failure time or exact failure count across executable versions.
